segments.activity: Model the close reading of the anchor quotation using the written think-aloud below.
segments.script: First, meaning. I read “On Saturday morning Elizabeth and Mr. Collins met for breakfast a few minutes before the others appeared” slowly and put it in my own words: On Saturday morning, Elizabeth and Mr. Collins meet at breakfast a few minutes before the others come down. Next, craft. I notice the precise timing, which sets up an awkward private moment for Collins's formal goodbyes. The strongest word is “minutes”: the brief gap gives Collins just enough time for a speech. Then, effect. Why does Austen mention that Elizabeth and Collins met before the others? My answer: The moment lets Collins make his pompous farewell, boasting of his happy home; Elizabeth must listen politely to the man whose proposal she refused.
